input: root is absent or a finite acyclic binary-search tree with n distinct node objects and no shared child nodes. Inorder node values are nondecreasing safe integers. Each node is an ordinary mutable object with writable data fields val, left and right; every child is another node or the absent value (None in Python, null in JavaScript). All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. Python integers are plain int values, excluding bool; node identity keys, when used, are opaque id values.
return: The original leftmost node, or the absent value for an empty tree. Following right pointers visits exactly the original nodes in their original inorder sequence; every left pointer and the final right pointer are absent.
mutation_aliasing: Input tree and all original links and identities remain unchanged. Returns an entirely fresh right-only chain of TreeNode objects in inorder-value order; all new left links are None and no output node aliases input.
numeric: Node values are only observed through the BST precondition, not arithmetically changed. Stack counts and indices are bounded by n. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n+1) time, O(h+1) traversal stack and O(n) explicitly allocated output nodes; no recursion. Full TreeNode constructor and caller are charged.
